Our results are slightly different from those presented in the scientific article. The regression equations and the ANOVA values are not exactly the same because we used a simpler statistical method and excluded some incomplete experimental conditions (ID3 and REP3).

However, the main conclusions are similar.

In our graph, movement time increases with the Index of Difficulty (ID) in all three groups. However, the increase is much stronger in the patient group (slope = 0.861) than in the age-matched group (slope = 0.176) and the young group (slope = 0.135).

This result is consistent with Figure 3 of the article, where the patient group also shows a much steeper regression slope than the two healthy groups.

Furthermore, our ANOVA shows a significant Group × ID interaction (F(2,48) = 11.58, p < 0.001). This confirms that the effect of task difficulty on movement time differs between groups.

Therefore, although the numerical results are different, our simpler analysis leads to the same main scientific conclusion :  Increasing task difficulty has a much stronger effect on movement time in patients with stroke than in healthy participants.
